title: Repair Cursor Pyright stall on ssot_checkout
objective: Stop the persistent Cursor status-bar and notification text N files to analyze plus Unable to open by (1) not creating .cursor-commands on ssot_checkout so Cursor Pyright cannot enumerate the second ~/.cursor-governance tree, and (2) pinning cursorpyright.analysis.include to the existing [tool.pyright] include list. Do not edit biome.json or the Biome extension. The diagnosed emitter is anysphere.cursorpyright, not biomejs.biome.
success_criteria: setup_workspace_symlinks.sh does not create .cursor-commands when classify_workspace_kind is ssot_checkout, and removes a pre-existing link on that kind
ops/scripts/tests/test_workspace_kind.sh or test_workspace_rules_overlay.sh PASSes a new ssot_checkout case that fails if .cursor-commands is created
environment/ide/settings.python.json sets cursorpyright.analysis.include to the same roots as pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] include, autoSearchPaths false, and shouldImportPylanceSettings never
After install_ide_profile merge, .vscode/settings.json carries those three keys; biome.json is byte-identical to HEAD

Cursor Pyright Output after Restart Server does not list files under .cursor-commands or ~/.cursor-governance as workspace sources; the files-to-analyze spinner clears on this checkout with only markdown tabs open
make pr-check PASSes against .pre-commit-config.yaml on the changed-file set

in: prove step: Restart Server + Output Cursor - Pyright
out: biome.json and biomejs.biome extension install or uninstall
pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] rewrite (exclude already lists .cursor-commands; file is additive_only)
restoring WIP/8-29-26/PEC/PEC-repair-pipeline.md or closing editor tabs
make campaign Program Lock PE overlay

pre_validation.command_or_action: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse HEAD && test -L .cursor-commands && python3 -c 'import os; print(os.path.realpath(".cursor-commands"))'
pre_validation.pass_criteria: branch main; HEAD recorded; .cursor-commands realpath is $HOME/.cursor-governance and not this workspace

pre_validation.command_or_action: rg -F 'files to analyze' ~/.cursor/extensions/anysphere.cursorpyright-1.0.12/dist/server.js; rg -F 'files to analyze' ~/.cursor/extensions/biomejs.biome-3.7.1-universal/out/main.js; pgrep -lf biomejs || true
pre_validation.pass_criteria: exact string present only in cursorpyright; biome main.js has no match; no biome LSP process

todos.task: In setup_workspace_symlinks.sh, classify workspace kind and treat ssot_checkout the same as ssot for .cursor-commands only: remove an existing link and do not create one. Consumers still get the link. Leave .cursor/plans and plugin wiring unchanged.
todos.anchor: C10 — never create a self-alias when wiring the SSOT clone itself
todos.shared_root_cause: sessionStart created .cursor-commands on a second governance clone; Pyright follows that symlink into a full second tree

todos.task: Add an ssot_checkout fixture case to the existing symlink/kind tests so setup_workspace_symlinks.sh fails the test if it creates .cursor-commands on an identity-tree checkout.

Add cursorpyright.analysis.include matching pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] include (conftest.py, ops, environment, skills, tools, workflows). Set cursorpyright.analysis.autoSearchPaths to false and cursorpyright.shouldImportPylanceSettings to never. Keep the existing exclude list. Do not edit biome.json.
todos.shared_root_cause: workspace settings have exclude only; autoSearchPaths defaults true so enumeration still walks extra trees

todos.task: Run install_ide_profile.sh on this workspace so .vscode/settings.json receives the new cursorpyright keys. Confirm biome.json is unchanged versus HEAD.

Run the kind tests and make pr-check. Restart Cursor Pyright. Confirm Output Cursor - Pyright does not enumerate .cursor-commands, and the files-to-analyze spinner is gone with only markdown editors open.

doc_root_surface_impact.reason: Section 11 already states ssot_checkout must not require consumer .cursor-commands; this plan implements that sentence in setup_workspace_symlinks.sh
No constitution change; symlink law already forbids SSOT self-alias and does not require the link on a second clone
README already names settings.python.json as the Python analysis payload; new keys live in that file
Biome is not the diagnosed emitter; leave the file untouched

disconfirming_questions: If after removing .cursor-commands the spinner still shows 13-plus files with only markdown tabs open, is a different language server or Cursor indexer the emitter?
If a consumer repo loses .cursor-commands because classify_workspace_kind mis-labels it as ssot_checkout, do slash commands break?
If [tool.pyright] include already limits enumeration, does adding vscode include change nothing and leave the stall intact?
assumed_false_ifs: anysphere.cursorpyright remains the owner of the files-to-analyze string
This folder remains ssot_checkout (realpath != $HOME/.cursor-governance, identity files present)
Consumers are not identity trees (no CANONICAL_LAW.md + AUTONOMY_MANIFEST + RULES-MANIFEST + check_governance_wiring.sh set)
stress_test.blast_radius: sessionStart wiring on every Cursor-Governance worktree or second clone; consumer repos unchanged if kind classification stays correct. Pyright completion scope shrinks to the include list (already the [tool.pyright] contract). Biome format-on-save for JS/TS/JSON is untouched.
stress_test.rollback: Revert setup_workspace_symlinks.sh and the test insertion. Revert environment/ide/settings.python.json. Re-run install_ide_profile.sh to restore .vscode/settings.json. Recreate .cursor-commands on this checkout only if a consumer workflow needs it (it is gitignored).
